# Workflow Design Critique

## Verdict

- status: approve_with_changes
- summary: The candidate applies Temporal as an orchestration/control plane, retains exact trajectory/workspace outside history in its recommended lane, and treats dispatch and physical termination as separate authorities. No critical or high design contradiction was identified. This remains a conditional proposal with open owner choices and unimplemented distributed proofs, not production readiness. Full contract finding ledger is contract.md.

The installed temporal-workflow-design-critic SKILL.md, rubric.md, checklist.md and decision-guide.md were applied by shell read. No native Claude Skill invocation is claimed. Temporal:temporal-developer Python/determinism/versioning references were also consulted. Ten independent successful Temporal Docs connector calls and Atlas SDK/features/canary reads support the review. Source captures are contract-source-identities.json.

## Top Issues

1. [medium] Exact trajectory/metadata/accepted-receipt composition remains unqualified.
   - Why: Public Preview claim check and a local conditional SDK adapter do not jointly guarantee native recovery, whole-tree fidelity or independent host-loss preservation.
   - Evidence: INV-5/A-60/A-61/A-63; R1/R3/R5/D5 in contract.md.
   - Required disposition: existing M1 P2/P2-S and M2 P4/P5 plus M3 P6-S. Classification ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION.

2. [medium] Entity dispatch authority needs real service/admin/lifecycle proof.
   - Why: server Update deduplication is per run; a durable successful reply must not become another spawn permit. Ledger deletion/reset/expiry or old authority rollback can invalidate the composition.
   - Evidence: INV-5/A-62/A-68; message-handler/entity patterns and features deduplication source.
   - Required disposition: existing P1-T/P2-I/P8-S/P9-S; preserve status/outcome-only duplicate replies and actual owned scheduling. Classification ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION.

3. [medium] Deployment fault/retention/load/version choices remain open.
   - Why: matched storage and authoritative physical termination depend on selected substrate and supported fault domain, while regional history rollback is explicitly outside the initial contract.
   - Evidence: BD-1..BD-4/BD-6, A-64/A-67/A-69; local Docker supervisor source and Temporal cancellation/idempotency sources.
   - Required disposition: M0/M2/M4; no platform or numeric threshold selected by reviewer. Classification OWNER-DECISION.

4. [info] Optional Mods and complete response escrow remain separately qualified.
   - Evidence: pinned declaration independently fetched and matching SHA; own-time/fail-open/stream boundaries read. Observation, native suspension/mapping and inference escrow have distinct acceptance.
   - Disposition: no baseline expansion; MG-0..MG-3 only after explicit lane selection.

## Category Review

### Temporal fit

Pass at design scope. Long-lived governed human/agent execution needs durable accepted control state, asynchronous decisions, park/recovery and component coordination. Large trajectory and workspace are not pushed indiscriminately through history.

### Workflows

Pass at design scope. IO is Activities; replay consumes recorded accepted results. Same-run Worker replacement is distinguished from new-run lifecycle operations. No Workflow retry policy is used to solve nonrepeatable side effects. Installed implementation must still prove replay and schema compatibility.

### Child Workflows

Not applicable to baseline. Separately started dispatch entity is preferred; optional child arrangement expressly requires independent lifecycle and confirmed start. Unsupported Claude child recovery remains denied.

### Activities

Pass as specified; inconclusive for implementation. Explicit deadlines/retries, heartbeat progress, protected wrapper claims and physical outcome/postimages replace assumptions of single execution. Original pending recovery and Bash use one attempt. Ordinary repeatable Write/Edit and special overlapping Edit retain canonical dispositions. Unknown Bash parks without synthetic model result. Physical cancellation/teardown is independent from Temporal cancellation.

### Signals

Not applicable as primary public mutation API; accepted writes use Updates. If Signals are introduced, retain equivalent dedup/volume/handler-handover constraints.

### Queries

Pass. Redacted state inspection supplies no acceptance or dispatch authority; reads cannot materialize a new accepted trajectory.

### Updates

Pass as contract; implementation inconclusive. Signed decisions validate identity/deadline/payload; lost response races and application dedup across CAN are tested. Entity duplicate request is status/outcome-only and entity owns scheduling. In-flight handlers drain before CAN.

### Workers and Task Queues

Pass for role separation; numeric capacity/HA/rate limits inconclusive pending BD-2/BD-4. Workflow/segment/effect/lifecycle roles are proposed, not discovered fleet facts. Shared queue compatibility/version registration and package/runtime storage admission require P9. No strict FIFO or arbitrary affinity guarantee is assumed.

### Timers / Schedules / Cron

Timers appropriate for bounded waits/deadlines; exact wake/deadline envelope is BD-4. Schedules/cron not applicable. No calendar mechanism is substituted for logical state wait.

### Data / Payloads / Converters

Pass architecture; implementation inconclusive. Raw opaque trajectory order/types and exact head are preserved, bounded history compared against external immutable payloads. Codec/failure conversion are explicit; Search Attributes exclude secrets. External Storage maturity/retention limitations remain visible. Cold workspace is not equated with automatic payload offload.

### Visibility

Pass. Queries and Search Attributes are discovery only; no eventually consistent index grants execution.

### Versioning

Pass contract; deployed compatibility inconclusive. Retained exact version lanes and replay/rollout/drain/migration tests gate resume. Worker deployment pins do not prove Claude engine/SDK compatibility. No unannounced SDK floor promotion.

### Long-running execution

Pass contract; capacity inconclusive pending BD-4/P9-S. CAN carries bounded accepted receipts, decisions, dedup, claims/tombstones and park state after handler drain. Earlier objects retain/reanchor through allowed recovery windows. No active uncontained execution crosses handover.

### Sessions and worker-specific routing

Go Sessions not applicable to Python. Reattachment may specialize attachment/routing only after explicit qualification; no session/host affinity replaces durability.

### Side effects

Pass contract. Nonrepeatable external actions remain protected Activities, with uncertainty parked. No SideEffect API acts as a general integration hook.

### Storage optimization

Pass contract; measured growth/retention inconclusive. Recommended bounded head plus blobs limits history; entity tombstone/index/restore growth gets P9-S. No infinite handover payload or automatic external GC is assumed.

## Open Questions

- BD-1: Which host/storage/service failures and accepted progress losses are offered?
- BD-2: Which exact platform, installed versions, physical terminal authority, storage and security owners?
- BD-3: Which live/park/reset/retention/nonrollback/administrative policy?
- BD-4: Which numeric duration/concurrency/payload/history/storage/SLO envelope?
- BD-5: Is confidential execution required, and against which adversary?
- BD-6: Is this protocol extension adopted; which optional native/escrow lane is offered?

These are recorded owner decisions, not reviewer requests for additional authorization.

## Checklist Result

All checklist items assessed; pass means adequate stated design contract, not an implemented test result.

| Group | pass | inconclusive | not_applicable | fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflows | fit, determinism, replay/versioning contract, history strategy, IDs, timeout posture, failures, no unjustified Workflow retry | actual replay/version qualification | none | none |
| Child Workflows | optional independent lifecycle constraint | actual optional child lifecycle if selected | baseline child use/count/communication | none |
| Activities | idempotency/ambiguity contract, granularity, heartbeat, reference payloads, intentional retries/timeouts, cancellation contract | physical/native fidelity, numerical settings, actual storage/confinement | local Activities; polling loop not proposed | none |
| Signals | dedup/handler rules inherited if used | chosen Signal rate if later introduced | primary Signal API/heavy handlers | none |
| Queries | read-only appropriate inspection | runtime availability/transport measurements | none | none |
| Updates | deterministic/idempotent contract, validation, scope, application dedup | actual gateway/runtime/CAN race proof | none | none |
| Workers/queues | intentional roles, valid ordering posture, version compatibility contract | worker count HA, registrations, rate/concurrency limits | none | none |
| Timers/schedules | relative waits/deadline semantics | numeric envelope | schedules/overlap/jitter/backfill/cron | none |
| Data/visibility | explicit converter/codec, nonsecret attributes, eventual consistency boundary, exact reference authority | codec/key/failure proof and measured sizes | cross-language datetimes not proposed | none |
| Versioning/long-running | replay strategy, CAN state/dedup/timer/authority carry contract | installed compatibility, retention, capacity, retirement proof | patch mechanism not selected | none |

Precedent conclusions: sanctioned smaller primitives; partial composed state/dispatch/handover mechanisms; none_found complete distributed original-pending/physical-fencing composition and optional complete inference escrow. Exact source references and corrective provenance are in contract.md. Independent contract verdict recommendation CONDITIONAL, exit test met with zero material core/remedy defects.
